intro: Rules for the seven playable classes, taken from the developer changelog. No D2 Survivors build guides are published yet, so this page does not recommend builds. The game changes often.
classesNote: The game site describes all seven heroes. They are Amazon, Sorceress, Necromancer, Paladin, Barbarian, Druid and Assassin. Warlock is not in the game.

general.title: Skill slots
paragraphs: A run starts as in D2, with only Attack and your starting weapon. The first card comes at once: a first skill from each skill tree, so all six skill slots are yours to fill.
A run started on Nightmare or Hell has its skill and passive slots from the start: 8 and 8 on Nightmare, 10 and 10 in Hell.
An earlier build said each difficulty adds two more skill slots and two more passive slots.

cites.quote: A run starts as in D2, with only Attack and your starting weapon, and your first card comes at once: a first skill from each skill tree, so all six skill slots are yours to fill
A run started on Nightmare or Hell has its skill and passive slots from the start: 8 and 8 on Nightmare, 10 and 10 in Hell
Two more skill and passive slots each difficulty

general.title: +skills, passives and auras
paragraphs: +skills on gear raise passives and auras too.
Evolved skills grow with +skills like the skills they replace. The changelog does not name which skill each evolved skill replaces.

cites.quote: +skills on gear raise passives and auras too
Evolved skills grow with +skills like the skills they replace

general.title: Late-run chests
paragraphs: Champions' and uniques' chests give level-ups through Act II and now and then in Act III, then stat points or +1 to a skill tree. The build fills in Acts IV and V.

cites.quote: Champions' and uniques' chests give level-ups through Act II and now and then in Act III, then stat points or +1 to a skill tree: the build fills in Acts IV-V

general.title: Lowering resistance
paragraphs: -% to Enemy Resistance lowers a monster's resistance, as in D2, instead of adding damage.
Monsters resist each element by D2's numbers, and immunities break only as D2's do: Amplify Damage, Decrepify, Lower Resist and Conviction lower resistances, a fifth as much on an immune.

general.title: Life stolen
paragraphs: Life Stolen goes by the damage a monster takes: less from physically resistant ones, none from immunes.

cites.quote: Life Stolen goes by the damage a monster takes: less from physically resistant ones, none from immunes

general.title: Required level
paragraphs: The changelog flipped this on the same day. The later line is the one that still stands: gear works at any level again. An item's Required Level is shown, but it no longer holds the item back.
The earlier line that day said gear asks its D2 Required Level again: you can wear it at any level, but above yours it shows red and gives nothing until you reach it.

cites.quote: Gear works at any level again: an item's Required Level is shown, but it no longer holds the item back
Gear asks its D2 Required Level again: wear it at any level, but above yours it shows red and gives nothing until you reach it

general.title: New weapon bases
paragraphs: New bases: crossbows, spears, polearms and more. The changelog does not say these belong to one class.

cites.quote: New bases: crossbows, spears, polearms and more

paragraphs: Dodge, Avoid and Evade work as in D2: Dodge and Avoid while she stands still, Evade while she moves, never all three at once.

cites.quote: The Amazon's Dodge, Avoid and Evade work as in D2: Dodge and Avoid while she stands still, Evade while she moves, never all three at once

tip.label: Fan tip, not a changelog rule
paragraphs: For a straightforward first run, try Barbarian and choose Double Swing when the skill choices appear.

Attacks such as Double Swing fire automatically, so focus on making room around enemies and collecting nearby drops. As you level up, read the choices and select an upgrade that supports your current skills.
tip.note: Fan beginner guide. Gameplay observations dated 18 Oct 2026 on that page.
